# Benchmark review — 2026-09-07

*Historical record. k6 and the shell drivers named below were removed on 2026-09-19; the pipelines now live in `.sql` and run through shellfs, and load is generated by `bench/loadgen.py`. The measurements and methodology here are left exactly as they were recorded.*

> **Remediation status, updated 2026-09-07.** The review below is a dated
> baseline, recorded before live listeners or Postgres were started. Its three
> highest-priority harness issues are now fixed: result directories are
> immutable, worker and connection budgets are recorded and equalized, and the
> report rejects cells without complete measurement-stage latency and
> commit/ack evidence. The report regression test now asserts parsed VUs,
> sample counts, and quantiles. See [the final smoke record](FINAL_SMOKE_2026_09_07.md)
> for the controlled isolated runs and their limits.

> A focused eight-worker write regression has passed after those fixes. The
> final four-stack smoke is run only from the consolidated build and is recorded
> in the linked document; this historical review remains unchanged below.

Reviewed the current working tree, including the core runner, SQL report, FastAPI
mirror, LLM gateway routes/scenario, and fanout routes. The formerly documented
`quackapi-wt/llm-bench` worktree is absent. This review makes no fresh throughput
claim: no shared Postgres data was truncated and no benchmark listeners were started.

## Fixed

- `report.sql`: `NTILE(100)` bucket maxima were labeled as percentiles. This is
  wrong for small or uneven sample counts: three observations produced only p1–p3;
  150 observations labeled the 100th value as p50 instead of the 75th. The report now
  uses native `quantile_disc` for nearest-rank p1–p100 and no longer loads the
  unused `stats_duck` extension.
- `routes.sql`: the rows workload now includes `ORDER BY id`, matching
  `fastapi_app.py`. Previously only FastAPI paid for deterministic ordering, and
  the two responses were not guaranteed to contain the same rows.
- `serve_quackapi.sh`: replaced the nonexistent 64-connection string substitution
  with an explicit startup emitter. Both worker configurations now emit their
  intended Postgres-extension pool, acquisition mode, and DuckDB thread settings.
- `bench_config.py`, runner, and FastAPI app: share one `PG_DSN`, including the
  QuackAPI attachment and direct `pg_dsn` route backend. Component environment
  settings are URL-escaped; an explicit DSN takes precedence. SQL literals are
  separately escaped. The report does not print credentials.
- `run.sh`: occupied ports now cause an error. Cleanup signals only the process
  group created for this launch, with bounded TERM-to-KILL escalation. Removed
  the obsolete adjacent-port sweep and corrected the proxy description.

## Verification performed

Executed the actual updated report through the local Quack service against
isolated generated CSV fixtures. The only report substitutions were its input
filename and capturing its final pivot as a temporary table. Each fixture also
included a warmup latency of 999999 and a non-latency metric to test filtering.

| Measured observations | Expected p1 / p50 / p95 / p99 / p100 | Result |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 | PASS |
| 3 | 1 / 2 / 3 / 3 / 3 | PASS |
| 101 | 2 / 51 / 96 / 100 / 101 | PASS |
| 150 | 2 / 75 / 143 / 149 / 150 | PASS |

Every fixture additionally asserted the correct retained sample count and exactly
100 percentile rows. `parser_tools.is_parsable` accepted the report. Fixtures are
`/tmp/quackapi-astra-report-{one,three,uneven,uneven150}-20260907.csv.gz`; they contain no
production data. The ordering change was reviewed against the FastAPI query;
the Postgres-backed route was not executed in this review.

Additional isolated regression checks passed:

- `bash bench/test_harness.sh`: actual SQL emitter at one/eight workers, quoted
  shared DSN in attachment and server startup, runner psql DSN propagation,
  refusal of an occupied-port stub, and real owned-process-group cleanup while
  preserving an unrelated process. Creates no HTTP listener or database connection.
- `python3 bench/test_bench_config.py`: three tests covering defaults, explicit
  DSN precedence, reserved credential characters, and IPv6 hosts.
- `bash -n` passed for the runner, QuackAPI launcher, and shell regression test.

The commands above were executed through Quack's shellfs reader. No live Postgres
connection or extension startup was attempted, so actual backend compatibility
still needs a controlled smoke run before trusting new performance comparisons.

## Highest-priority remaining issues

1. **Failed responses can appear as competitive latency.** Core scenarios use
   always-true check thresholds; `run.sh` keeps nonzero k6 exits as warnings.
   `report.sql` displays duration samples without status/check validity, request
   rate, timeout counts, or interruption counts. The write rowcheck
   writes two counts without asserting equality. Preserve invalid cells but
   label them invalid and exclude them from winner calculations. Report attempted
   and successful throughput separately. Distinguish an interrupted warmup write
   that committed from a confirmed lost acknowledged write.
2. **Worker/resource comparisons still need controlled budgets.**
   The broken settings substitution is fixed, but QuackAPI sets eight HTTP workers
   per process at w8, while FastAPI retains 32 thread and PG pool slots per process
   (`fastapi_app.py`). Set explicit shared budgets, verify effective native libpq
   and Postgres-extension pool values, verify every requested worker is alive,
   and compare both equal-resource and separately tuned configurations.
3. **Previous evidence is deleted.** `run.sh` removes the entire results
   directory. Use unique run directories, a manifest recording source/build hashes,
   dependency versions, effective worker/pool settings, commands, and trial order.
   Keep raw CSV, summaries, server logs, errors, and rowcheck artifacts together.

## Performance experiments that would support decisions

- Use repeated trials with alternating/randomized stack order and deterministic
  request inputs. Current fixed stack order and random IDs/prompts can confound
  cache state, thermal behavior, and upstream work.
- Retain the closed-loop VU sweep, and add fixed arrival-rate sweeps with offered
  versus achieved rate, dropped iterations, timeouts, p50/p95/p99/max, CPU, RSS,
  queue depth, connection reuse, and per-worker distribution. A saturated
  closed-loop client reduces offered load and can hide queueing behavior.
- For blocking upstream routes, sweep service time and concurrency around the
  worker limit. Test bounded admission, queue timeout/cancellation, and fair
  connection scheduling before simply raising the thread count. Compare against
  the upstream directly and the same route without outbound I/O.
- Separate no-log, deferred-log, and equally durable-log LLM comparisons. FastAPI
  BackgroundTasks and QuackAPI durable enqueue provide different guarantees.
  Verify sink delivery and crash recovery separately from response latency.
- LLM code should reject non-2xx upstream responses and validate semantic output
  before recording metrics. `scenarios/llm.js:72` clamps negative overhead to zero;
  retain signed residuals and flag inconsistent/missing upstream timing instead.
  Pin prompts, model identity, token limits, and model warm/cold state; add streaming
  time-to-first-token and cancellation workloads when that feature is supported.
- Fanout should assert both fanout count and aggregate content, exercise upstream
  errors/timeouts, and cap per-request fanout. Test memory growth with concurrency;
  width-sized scan buffers make latency alone an incomplete result.

## Historical results

`LLM_GATEWAY.md` records a fixed-latency mock experiment, explicitly not live Ollama.
It reports 32-worker tail collapse and improvement with 128 workers. Those are
historical document claims, not reproduced measurements in this review. The checked
benchmark directory contains no retained raw results validating them. Its inference
that this also explains the older Postgres ATTACH issue remains a hypothesis.
The older benchmark skill describes a different pooling investigation and a now
absent private harness; do not merge those narratives into one measured experiment.
